en: The Questions of King Milinda, Chapter on Investigation: 12.
The Question on the Characteristic of Consciousness (Viññāṇalakkhaṇapañha)
“Venerable Nāgasena, what is the characteristic of consciousness?
“Consciousness, Great King, has the characteristic of cognizing.
“Just as, great king, a city guard sitting at the crossroads in the center of the city might see a man coming from the eastern direction,
see a man coming from the southern direction, see a man coming from the western direction,
and see a man coming from the northern direction;”
In the same way, great king, whatever form a person sees with the eye, that he cognizes by means of consciousness;
whatever sound he hears with the ear, that he cognizes by means of consciousness;
whatever odor he smells with the nose, that he cognizes by means of consciousness.
And whatever taste one tastes with the tongue, that one cognizes by means of consciousness;

and whatever tangible object one touches with the body, that one cognizes by means of consciousness; and whatever mental phenomenon one cognizes with the mind, that one cognizes by means of consciousness.
Thus, Great King, consciousness has the characteristic of cognizing.”
Thus ends the twelfth problem: on the characteristic of consciousness.
